target.title: fix: route iOS OpenAI realtime Talk through WebRTC
target.body:
Related: #91007

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iOS users trying to use OpenAI Realtime Talk could see the app enter the Gateway Relay path even though the Gateway advertised a WebRTC realtime configuration. In local reproduction, the app showed the OpenAI realtime config as Gateway Relay and the relay session failed early with `session.error` / `Unknown Talk session` before audio append or close could complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already carries the requested realtime transport. This change makes the iOS Talk route honor OpenAI Realtime configs with `transport: "webrtc"` by using the existing native WebRTC session path instead of mapping them to Gateway Relay.

Explicit `gateway-relay` remains on the relay path, and provider websocket, non-OpenAI realtime, managed-room, and unsupported-brain configs are intentionally kept out of the native OpenAI WebRTC route. The app-selected OpenAI Realtime fallback now also defaults to Native WebRTC, clears stale non-OpenAI realtime provider/model/voice state when it overrides a previous config, and preserves explicit OpenAI voice-picker overrides. Native WebRTC audio sessions now also honor and refresh the Talk speakerphone preference.

## User Impact

iOS Talk can now use the intended Native WebRTC path for OpenAI Realtime configurations that request WebRTC, while existing relay/provider-websocket behavior remains available for configurations that explicitly need it. This prevents OpenAI WebRTC configs from being routed through the relay-only session flow that can fail before audio is processed.

## Evidence

- Before/after route proof:
  - before: iOS entered `Gateway Relay` for an OpenAI Realtime config that requested WebRTC, followed by early relay session failure with `session.error` / `Unknown Talk session`
  - after: the same config selects `Native WebRTC`; the screenshot below shows `Configured` = `GPT Realtime 2.0` and `Active now` = `GPT Realtime 2.0 · Native WebRTC`
  - scope: this proves route selection only, not a completed physical-device audio/transcript round trip
  - Inspectable proof image: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/proof/pr-98563-native-webrtc/proof/pr-98563/ios-talk-native-webrtc-20260701T1153.png
  - Proof branch: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/tree/proof/pr-98563-native-webrtc/proof/pr-98563
  - SHA-256: `87b9462a5a3246f614ec5acae4bae5e543a6e4eddfadabf2adfb7c172a5c86a9`
  - Visual readback: top of Talk screen shows `main · GPT Realtime 2.0`; status pill says `Listening`; the central session card says `Listening` / `Native WebRTC`; the Voice mode card says `Configured GPT Realtime 2.0` and `Active now GPT Realtime 2.0 · Native WebRTC`.
- Maintainer repair on exact head `059023e7800350bd59d922b81465c5004f90509d`:
  - case-insensitive OpenAI provider matching now preserves an explicitly configured OpenAI voice
  - explicit `gateway-relay` and `provider-websocket` ownership survives the OpenAI provider override, while a non-OpenAI `webrtc` config can become native OpenAI WebRTC
  - the speakerphone preference no longer overrides headphones, Bluetooth, CarPlay, AirPlay, USB, HDMI, line-out, unknown, or indeterminate output routes
  - Talk audio categories preserve Bluetooth HFP/A2DP and AirPlay; route-preference changes no longer increment WebRTC's audio-session activation count, and stop balances only the activation owned by that session
  - regression coverage includes whitespace/case-normalized provider input with the `marin` voice
  - Talk and iOS platform docs now distinguish native WebRTC from gateway relay, provider WebSocket, and non-realtime native speech
- Fresh structured Codex autoreview
  - initial passes found provider-websocket, non-OpenAI default, non-OpenAI explicit WebRTC, unsupported-brain routing, stale provider/model/voice, and speakerphone-preference edge cases; fixed with regression tests or scoped implementation changes
  - local lifecycle repair review: clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.94
  - branch-wide review against current `origin/main`: clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.90; the only later change was generated native-i18n line-number synchronization
- `xcodebuild -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=287E61C4-E15A-4794-A8DF-3E6AC37AAF97' -only-testing:OpenClawTests/TalkModeManagerTests test`
  - passed: 32 tests in `TalkModeManagerTests`
- `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawLogicTests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17,OS=26.5' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ARCHS=arm64 ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES VALID_ARCHS=arm64`
  - passed: 7 tests in `TalkConfigParsingTests`
- `xcodebuild build -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17,OS=26.5' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ARCHS=arm64 ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES VALID_ARCHS=arm64`
  - passed
- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeGatewayConfig.swift apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession.swift apps/ios/Tests/TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift apps/ios/Tests/TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests.swift`
  - passed
- `swiftlint lint --config apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeGatewayConfig.swift apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession.swift apps/ios/Tests/TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift apps/ios/Tests/TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests.swift`
  - passed with 0 violations
- `git diff --check`
  - passed
- `pnpm native:i18n:check`
  - passed after synchronizing six generated line-number locations in `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`; no localized source text changed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/nodes/talk.md docs/platforms/ios.md`, MDX syntax check, and docs link audit
  - passed; `broken_links=0`

Physical-device gate:

- A fresh simulator run paired successfully and selected the OpenAI Native WebRTC route, but the app correctly rejected starting Talk with `Talk mode is not supported on the iOS simulator`.
- No physical iOS device was attached for this maintainer pass. Do not merge until a paired physical iPhone completes an audible input -> OpenAI Realtime -> transcript/audio response round trip.

Rebase note:

- Current `origin/main` includes adjacent iOS Talk Gateway speech changes from #98376. This patch was adapted onto the new `TalkModeRuntimeRoute` / `gatewayTalkSpeak` routing model instead of reverting that work.
- Xcode initially tested against a stale generated project that did not compile newly-added upstream `TalkGatewaySpeechClient.swift`; regenerating with `xcodegen generate` resolved that without adding project-file churn to this patch.

Additional exploratory run:

- Full `OpenClaw` scheme tests reached the Talk suites and both Talk suites passed, but the full run ended red from unrelated gateway/keychain persistence tests (`GatewayConnection*`, `GatewaySettingsStore*`, `KeychainStore*`) in this simulator environment.

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation and review were done with Codex, with local review findings addressed before publication.
